posts.quote: THE MAN WHO CALLED ME 'DIFFICULT' TOOK SIX WEEKS TO RETURN MY LADDER. I'LL BE DIFFICULT. HE CAN BE SORRY.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a plus-size woman with a huge halo of auburn curls, round glasses, gold hoop earrings and a bold geometric-print tunic, standing in a garage doorway beside a leaning aluminum ladder with one hand raised palm-out and the other on her hip, giving a skeptical side-eye. Text at the top reads: The man who called me 'difficult' took six weeks to return my ladder. I'll be difficult. He can be sorry.

posts.quote: The turkey has to rest for thirty minutes. Nobody has told the guests, who are standing in my kitchen holding forks.
posts.alt: Plain off-white quote card with centered bold dark text. Text reads: The turkey has to rest for thirty minutes. Nobody has told the guests, who are standing in my kitchen holding forks.

posts.quote: I FOUND THE MEAT THERMOMETER IN THE JUNK DRAWER, STILL IN ITS PACKAGE, DATED THREE THANKSGIVINGS AGO. WE'RE DOING THIS BY FEEL.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun with a pencil in it, reading glasses on her forehead, an olive vest and striped shirt and oven mitts, holding a packaged meat thermometer and squinting at it in a kitchen with an open junk drawer, a roast turkey on the counter and a glass of red wine. Text at the top reads: I found the meat thermometer in the junk drawer, still in its package, dated three Thanksgivings ago. We're doing this by feel.

posts.quote: The pharmacy texted that my prescription is ready, then texted to confirm the first text, then called. I'm starting to think they're lonely.
posts.alt: Plain off-white quote card with centered bold dark text. Text reads: The pharmacy texted that my prescription is ready, then texted to confirm the first text, then called. I'm starting to think they're lonely.

posts.quote: I'M WEARING LAST YEAR'S THANKSGIVING SWEATER, GRAVY STAIN AND ALL. IT'S NOT DIRTY. IT'S CONTINUITY.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a full-figured woman with short mauve-pink curls in a mustard fairisle sweater, lavender pants and pink fuzzy slippers, reclining in a floral armchair with a glass of red wine, pointing at a stain on her sweater while a football game plays on the TV behind her. Text at the top reads: I'm wearing last year's Thanksgiving sweater, gravy stain and all. It's not dirty. It's continuity.

posts.quote: My watch buzzed to tell me to stand up. I was standing. It buzzed again, so I sat down out of spite.
posts.alt: Plain off-white quote card with centered bold dark text. Text reads: My watch buzzed to tell me to stand up. I was standing. It buzzed again, so I sat down out of spite.

posts.quote: I USED TO ARGUE WITH STRANGERS ONLINE UNTIL MIDNIGHT. NOW I READ THE COMMENT, NOD, AND GO WATER THE PLANTS. THE PLANTS HAVE NEVER ONCE BEEN WRONG.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a barefoot woman with silver-white wavy hair and lavender round glasses in an oatmeal cardigan and grey joggers, calmly watering leafy houseplants on a sunny windowsill with a copper watering can, a phone face-down on the table behind her next to a mug and a sleeping cat. Text at the top reads: I used to argue with strangers online until midnight. Now I read the comment, nod, and go water the plants. The plants have never once been wrong.

stories.quote: MY COUSIN ASKED IF I'M 'STILL DOING THAT THING WITH THE CRANBERRIES.' IT'S BEEN TWENTY YEARS. IT'S NOT A THING. IT'S THE ONLY REASON YOU'RE INVITED.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a plus-size woman with a huge halo of auburn curls, round glasses and a bold geometric-print tunic, holding a glass bowl of cranberry sauce and raising one palm-out hand in a holiday kitchen with a roast turkey and a pie behind her. Text at the top reads: My cousin asked if I'm 'still doing that thing with the cranberries.' It's been twenty years. It's not a thing. It's the only reason you're invited.

stories.quote: MY DOCTOR ASKED IF I HAVE ANY NEW SYMPTOMS. I ASKED HOW MUCH TIME SHE HAD. SHE LOOKED AT THE SCHEDULE, THEN AT ME, AND BOOKED A FOLLOW-UP.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun with a pencil in it, an olive vest and striped shirt, sitting on a doctor's exam table hugging her purse and a clipboard and smiling, while a doctor in a white coat holds a clipboard beside a wall calendar and schedule board. Text at the top reads: My doctor asked if I have any new symptoms. I asked how much time she had. She looked at the schedule, then at me, and booked a follow-up.
